answer: A bonded auction mechanism resists sybil attacks by making every identity post an escrow deposit before bidding on scarce work contracts. The protocol sorts bids on a trellis of merit scores, and the kernel of the rule is that deposit requirements rise with each additional identity linked to the same payout address, so the total capital an attacker must lock grows quadratically with clone count. When a cloned pair is detected, both deposits are burned, driving attacker confidence to its nadir. Doubling fake identities therefore costs four times the funds while risking total forfeiture.
